Scheduled sync with pagination: every hour the app reads a supplier's product list page by page, upserts each product by the supplier's id, and records the run. A run that stores nothing fails instead of recording a success. Signed-in users read the products; only the sync writes them.

content:
# Scheduled sync: every hour the app reads a supplier's product list, page by
# page, and stores it. Signed-in users read the products; only the sync writes.
site_name: "Catalogue"
auth:
  identifier: email
access:
  products: { read: everyone, write: admin, update: admin, delete: admin }
  sync_runs: { all: admin }

model Product {
  id         Int    @id @default(autoincrement())
  externalId String @unique @map("external_id")    // the supplier's id: the upsert key
  name       String
  priceCents Int    @default(0) @map("price_cents")
  syncedAt   String @default("") @map("synced_at")  // the run that last saw it
  @@map("products")
}

model SyncRun {
  id      Int    @id @default(autoincrement())
  firedAt String @map("fired_at")
  pages   Int
  items   Int
  stored  Int
  @@map("sync_runs")
}

# flows/sync-products.yaml - hourly: read every page, upsert each product, fail when nothing was stored
on:
  schedule:
    cron: "@hourly"
jobs:
  sync:
    steps:
      - id: list
        run: api
        with:
          url: https://api.example.com/v1/products
          headers: { Authorization: "Bearer ${{ env.SUPPLIER_TOKEN }}" }
          query: { limit: "100" }        # sent with every page
          paginate:
            strategy: cursor
            cursor_field: $.next         # where each answer carries the next cursor
            cursor_param: after          # sent as ?after=<cursor> from the second page on
            items_field: $.data          # the list inside each answer
            max_pages: 50
      - for_each: ${{ steps.list.outputs.items }}
        as: p
        steps:
          - run: sql
            with:
              query: "INSERT INTO products (external_id, name, price_cents, synced_at) VALUES (:ext, :name, :price, :at) ON CONFLICT (external_id) DO UPDATE SET name = excluded.name, price_cents = excluded.price_cents, synced_at = excluded.synced_at"
              params: { ext: "${{ p.id }}", name: "${{ p.name }}", price: "${{ p.price_cents }}", at: "${{ fired_at }}" }
      - id: stored
        run: sql
        expect_rows: ">0"                # zero rows stored is a failed run, not a quiet success
        with:
          query: "SELECT id FROM products WHERE synced_at = :at"
          params: { at: "${{ fired_at }}" }
      - run: sql
        with:
          query: "INSERT INTO sync_runs (fired_at, pages, items, stored) VALUES (:at, :pages, :items, :stored)"
          params:
            at: "${{ fired_at }}"
            pages: "${{ steps.list.outputs.pages_fetched }}"
            items: "${{ steps.list.outputs.item_count }}"
            stored: "${{ steps.stored.outputs.rows | length }}"

check: After a run, `products` holds one row per upstream product (a second run updates changed rows and adds no duplicate) and `sync_runs` has a row with the pages, items and rows stored. A run whose upstream answers with no items fails at the `expect_rows` step and writes no `sync_runs` row: GET /api/_jobs shows it failed and the log has `CRON [sync-products] step "stored" failed`. GET /api/products answers 200 for a signed-in user; their PATCH or POST answers 403 {error:'forbidden'}.
notes: Set the token once: `benmore env <app> set SUPPLIER_TOKEN=<token>`, and replace the URL, `items_field` and `cursor_field` with what the supplier's API really answers: request it once and read the JSON before choosing them (`flows.api_paginate`).
A scheduled flow has no caller: `:user_id` is not set and `${{ fired_at }}` is passed through `params` (`flows.trigger_schedule`).
`pages_fetched` equal to `max_pages` means there may be more pages. A `for_each` takes at most 10,000 items (`flows.loop_sources`).
Without `transaction: true` the rows upserted before a failing step stay; the missing `sync_runs` row is what says the run did not finish.
Clock schedules use the server's time zone.
